title: Quantized fallthrough routing with backpressure buckets for multi-region SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Cross-region bursts cause tail latency violations even when aggregate capacity is sufficient. Existing geo-pin + latency-steering causes oscillation when capacity dips and falls back aggressively, leading to cascading circuit breaker trips and user-facing error spikes. Proposal: implement a 'quantized fallthrough' routing mode that assigns requests into discrete capacity buckets per region (low/med/high latency sensitivity). Each bucket has a backpressure occupancy metric (token/backlog count) and an associated circuit-breaker curve. Routing will prefer pinned regions for bucket-appropriate requests, but will 'fall through' to less-preferred regions only when the local bucket occupancy exceeds a soft threshold; aggressive shedding occurs when occupancy hits hard threshold. Key aspects: capacity-aware bucketization (per-model, per-instance), latency-tiered SLO mapping (SLO tier 1/2/3 mapped to preferential buckets), and predictive short-term EWMA backlog estimator to pre-emptively steer before hard trips. Goals: reduce SLO breaches during partial regional degradation, avoid mass fallback storms, and offer predictable unit economics by bounding cross-region egress.
acceptance_criteria: Routing respects SLO tier mapping for >99% of requests under normal load
During moderate regional capacity pressure (30-60% occupancy) fallthrough rate increases smoothly with no more than 10% spike in tail latency in destination regions
Hard-shed triggers limit overall request loss to <0.5% during severe overloads and prevent cascade failures
Ability to toggle quantized fallthrough per-customer and per-model with runtime config in Console
Integration tests covering synthetic regional node failures and spike workloads pass in CI
implementation_steps: Design data model for per-region bucket occupancy and expose a compact proto over routing plane
Add EWMA-based short-term backlog estimator and validate against production traces (1M requests sample)
Implement soft/hard threshold policy and circuit-breaker curves in the director service
Add fallthrough logic that respects SLO tier buckets and applies cost/egress tagging
Add metrics and tracing: bucket_occupancy, fallthrough_rate, predicted_backlog, shed_rate
Create canary rollout plan: 5% of traffic in US-east, synthetic failure tests, progressive ramp to 50%
Document runtime flags in Console and provide toggles per-client

notes: Trade-offs: quantized buckets simplify policy decisions and reduce oscillation, but can increase cross-region egress if soft thresholds are conservative. We prefer stable SLO adherence over minimal egress for initial launch.
Observability: dashboards will show per-bucket SLO attainment and a 'pressure map' heatmap across regions.
Rollout plan: start with low-risk models and customers, add telemetry to detect unintended latency cost increases before full roll.
